$comment: The icons contract. This file is data, not a JSON Schema meta-schema: it states the shape the consumer relies on and the placeholder vocabulary rules, so a mapping entry and a template can be checked against a written contract instead of against a renderer's behaviour. `schema_major` is the consumer-compatibility version (spine AD-12) and moves independently of the repo tag; raising it requires a MAJOR tag.

paths.note: Both roots are repo-local and relative to this repository's root. This file names no deployment path and no consumer destination (spine AD-2/AD-6). `vocabulary.json` is the role vocabulary of record and `ROLE-MIGRATION.md` the reviewed role proposal; neither is a mapping file and neither is loaded by a consumer.

shape.description: `icons/mappings/icons.yaml` is THE group map: a YAML document whose TOP-LEVEL KEYS are icon groups. A group is a logical name, not necessarily a directory: `battery`, `network` and `wifi-*` all live under `status-bar/`, addressed by their variant `template` paths. The only directory knob is the group's optional `template_dir`. `icons/mappings/defaults.yaml` is the exception: its top-level key is `defaults`, the group-independent COLOR_* vocabulary, not a group. No other mapping file may exist beside these two.

mapping_file.root: mapping of group name -> group entry
mapping_file.consumer: exactly one group map, `icons.yaml`, plus the vocabulary `defaults.yaml`. Per-group splitting is deliberately not supported: a consumer loads ONE mapping file, so a second group map would be a second source of truth that drifts. `make validate-icons` fails if any other `*.yaml` appears under `mappings/`. The six legacy per-concern files (battery, email-client, network, power-menu, wallpaper-selector, wlogout) were retired in v0.2.0 because they duplicated groups owned by `icons.yaml` and nothing loaded them.
mapping_file.companions: `vocabulary.json` (the declared role vocabulary) and `ROLE-MIGRATION.md` (the reviewed group/variant -> role proposal) live beside the two mapping files. They are contracts and documentation, not mappings: the consumer loads neither, they carry no templates, and the `*.yaml` single-manifest rule above is unchanged. `make validate-icons` reads `vocabulary.json` as the authority for mapping values and `ROLE-MIGRATION.md` as the coverage record.

group_entry.id: string — the group name; the key itself, unique within its mapping file
group_entry.template_dir: string — OPTIONAL directory under `templates_root` that variant templates are joined under; defaults to "." (the templates root itself). Must stay inside `templates_root`
group_entry.surface: string — OPTIONAL surface class the group's glyphs are composed for: `wallpaper`, `dark-glass` or `solid`. Inherited by every variant; a variant that paints its own container or sits on a different layer overrides it. Optional in the role-migration Phase A (declaring a surface is a render input, so Phase B declares the values); once declared, the validator holds `surface: wallpaper` variants to `on_backdrop` ink
group_entry.color_mappings: object — OPTIONAL COLOR_NAME -> value. The value MUST be a declared role in `mappings/vocabulary.json`; `colorN` carrier indices and producer aliases (`foreground`, `accent`, `accent-muted`, `warning`) are rejected, because their meaning is positional, not semantic
group_entry.variants: array — REQUIRED, at least one; see variant_entry
group_entry.consumer_metadata: `bar_mappings`, `output_dir` and `unsafe` are passed through by the consumer (AGS state -> variant tables, per-group output directory, unsafe-render flag). This repository ships them as data and `make validate-icons` does not interpret them.

variant_entry.name: string — REQUIRED, unique within the group; the selector a consumer asks for
variant_entry.template: string — REQUIRED path to the SVG RELATIVE TO THE GROUP'S TEMPLATE ROOT (`templates_root/<template_dir>`, where `template_dir` defaults to "."): forward slashes, no leading `/`, no `..`. The consumer joins it under that root — not under the mapping file's directory
variant_entry.output: string — REQUIRED; the rendered file name the consumer writes. A bare file name: no path separators, no `..`, no placeholder
variant_entry.surface: string — OPTIONAL per-variant override of the group's `surface`, same enum. Use it when the variant is not on the group's layer: a variant that paints its own filled container (`solid`), or a `system-*` copy that serves a panel instead of the bar (`dark-glass` vs `wallpaper`)
variant_entry.color_mappings: object — OPTIONAL per-variant override, highest priority in the merge

surface_classes.description: The composition layer a glyph is drawn for. It is the missing datum behind the legacy `colorN` pins: the same carrier index is fine on a panel and wrong over the wallpaper. A group declares its surface; a variant overrides it when it is not on the group's layer (a `system-*` panel copy, or a variant that paints its own container). Declaring a surface is a render input, so the role-migration Phase A adds the field and only Phase B sets the values.

contract.wallpaper: Composited directly over the wallpaper (floating bar glyph, full-screen wallpaper button). Glyph ink MUST resolve to `on_backdrop`. Decorative accents may use `primary`/`tertiary`/`error`, but the shape must still carry the state when they miss contrast.
contract.dark-glass: On a translucent sheet, `alpha(surface*, ~0.9)` over a transparent window. Use the on-surface / on-container family for that sheet (`on_surface`, `on_surface_variant`, `on_primary`, `on_primary_container`). `on_backdrop` is wrong here: no wallpaper band is behind the glyph.
contract.solid: On an opaque surface, field, or a container the variant paints itself. Use the on-surface / on-container family for that surface. `on_backdrop` is wrong here for the same reason as dark-glass.

surface_classes.phase_b_rule: Once a variant declares `surface: wallpaper`, every `COLOR_FOREGROUND` / `COLOR_JOIN` it resolves to MUST be `on_backdrop`. The validator enforces this only for declared surfaces, so the rule is vacuous in Phase A and live in Phase B.

placeholder_vocabulary.description: Placeholders are the only variable part of a template. The vocabulary is a contract: renaming a token breaks every consumer that supplies it, so a rename is a MAJOR change even though no file moved.
placeholder_vocabulary.syntax: {{COLOR_NAME}} — exactly two opening braces, the name, two closing braces, no whitespace inside, nothing else on the token
rules: Every token used by any .svg under a group's template directory MUST be declared in that group's `color_mappings` (or a variant override), or in `icons/mappings/defaults.yaml` (the group-independent vocabulary).

Every mapping VALUE (defaults, group or variant) MUST be a role declared in `icons/mappings/vocabulary.json`. `colorN` carrier indices and the producer aliases (`foreground`, `accent`, `accent-muted`, `warning`) are rejected: their meaning is positional or re-mapped, not semantic. The one exception is `phase_a_legacy_baseline` in `vocabulary.json`, an exact, shrink-only list of the pre-migration values that Phase B must empty.
Declaring a token no SVG uses is allowed (forward compatibility); `make validate-icons` reports it, it does not fail the tag.
No defaults, filters, conditionals or nesting inside a token: `{{COLOR_BG|#000}}`, `{{ COLOR_BG }}` and `{{{{...}}}}` are invalid.

A token is substituted by the CONSUMER at render time. No rendered SVG, no generated icon index and no palette state is ever committed here (spine AD-11), so a preview of this corpus lives in the consumer, not in this repository.
`output` values and mapping keys may not contain `{{`: a placeholder in a destination is not renderable by any consumer.

validation.make validate: The envelope: valid JSON, integer `schema_major`, and the `shape` / `placeholder_vocabulary` sections present (scripts/validate-catalog.py).
make validate-icons: `mappings/` holds exactly one group map (`icons.yaml`) plus the vocabulary (`defaults.yaml`); any other `*.yaml` fails, because the consumer loads one file and a split is a second source of truth
every `template:` in `icons.yaml` resolves to a real file under `icons/templates/<template_dir>/`
every `{{COLOR_*}}` token used by a template is declared in `defaults.yaml` or that group's / variant's `color_mappings`

every mapping VALUE is a role declared in `mappings/vocabulary.json`; `colorN` and aliases fail unless they are an exact entry in `phase_a_legacy_baseline`, and a baseline entry that no longer matches a live pin also fails (shrink-only ratchet)
`mappings/vocabulary.json` declares 50 Material roles plus `on_backdrop`, unique, with its source note and the three surface classes
any `surface` declared at group or variant level is one of `wallpaper | dark-glass | solid`, and a declared `surface: wallpaper` variant's ink resolves to `on_backdrop`
`mappings/ROLE-MIGRATION.md` names every group and variant in `icons.yaml` (the reviewed proposal cannot silently miss new art)
every SVG under `icons/templates/` parses as XML
every `variant.name` is unique within its group
every `output` is a bare file name and every `template` stays inside the templates root
reported_not_failed: a token declared for a group but unused by its templates (forward compatibility)
a group or variant with no `surface` declared yet (Phase A: the field is optional; Phase B declares the values)
validation.make validate-content: The content class: `content/wallpapers/wallpapers.tar.gz` holds a top-level `default.png`, every `*.theme` is non-empty, and no archive member escapes the archive root.
validation.new_work: No schema file existed anywhere in the dotfiles corpus before this repository. The shape above is written from what the consumer's loader already expects (icon_templates_renderer `YamlIconConfigLoader` + `PathResolutionService`), and since v0.2.0 it is enforced against the shipped corpus by `make validate-icons`, not only stated.
